html:
SMTO-AUT-0032 — Your Google account needs to be reconnected

GUID: 455945c2-75d2-54c5-a49a-66263a1134dc
Slug: google-reauthorization-required
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • SMTO's saved access to this Google account expired, was removed, or was disconnected, so SMTO can't renew it on its own. The request that needed Google didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to reconnect the same Google account under the same name, for example by typing @ in the message box and picking that account. Using the same name keeps the account's existing setup and the access you already approved.
  2. Open the Google link SMTO gives you and sign in with the same email address as before. SMTO refuses a different Google account here, so it can't accidentally act as someone else.
  3. Approve the access Google lists, wait for the page to say you're connected, then send your request again. Approving gives SMTO fresh access that it can keep renewing on its own.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in page says your email is connected, and your request runs without asking you to sign in.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the Google account entry or connect a different account to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The saved Google account has no usable refresh grant: the refresh token is missing, Google rejected it with invalid_grant, or the account's authorization_state requires reconnection.

What this means

  • A usable refresh grant is missing or rejected, or the saved account authorization state requires reconnection. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • A usable refresh grant is missing or rejected, or the saved account authorization state requires reconnection.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare refresh availability, provider invalid_grant status and saved authorization state; a transient transport error is a separate category.

How to fix it

  • Reconnect the same account_key through auth.google_connect (or google_calendar.connect / google_drive.connect) with the same google_oauth_app; the stored refresh authorization is missing, expired or revoked, and the account is marked reauthorization_required. The same Google subject must sign in, since a different subject is refused as account_key_conflict.
  • Reconnect the same account key through auth.google_connect. The saved refresh authorization is missing, expired or revoked.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • Reconnecting the intended account restores a valid grant and required feature access.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
